examples.text: Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist any change in its motion!
When you shake a ketchup bottle and suddenly stop your hand, the sauce keeps moving down because of inertia!
Inertia is the natural tendency of an object to resist any change in its motion!
An object at rest will stay perfectly still and at rest unless a force pushes or pulls it to make it move!
When all forces on an object are balanced (net force is zero), its motion doesn't change, according to Newton's first law!
Newton's first law says an object at rest stays at rest, and a moving object keeps moving, unless an unbalanced force acts on it!
Even at constant speed, an object in circular motion has an acceleration pointing toward the center because its velocity direction keeps changing!
An object's acceleration is always in the direction of the net force! A forward net force speeds it up, backward slows it down, and sideways makes it turn.
Even at constant speed, an object in circular motion has an acceleration pointing toward the center because its velocity direction keeps changing!
An object's acceleration is always in the direction of the net force! A forward net force speeds it up, backward slows it down, and sideways makes it turn.

Is a car accelerating when it turns?

Yes! Acceleration is any change in speed or direction. So a car speeding up, slowing down, or turning a corner is all accelerating!
In physics, acceleration means ANY change in speed OR direction! A force can speed up, slow down, or turn an object. Even a car turning at constant speed is accelerating!
The equation for Newton's second law is F=ma (force = mass x acceleration)!
One newton (1 N) is the exact force that gives a 1-kilogram mass an acceleration of 1 m/s²!
The equation for Newton's second law is F=ma (force = mass x acceleration)!
One newton (1 N) is the exact force that gives a 1-kilogram mass an acceleration of 1 m/s²!
Newton's second law means acceleration equals force divided by mass (F=ma). This means a heavier object needs more force to achieve the same acceleration as a lighter one!

Why does a carabao need more force for a loaded cart?

Bigger mass means smaller acceleration! For the same force (F = ma), a heavy loaded cart accelerates slower than an empty one.

Did you know every action has a reaction?

Newton's third law says that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction!

What is the secret behind Newton's third law of motion?

It says that for every single action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction!
The action and reaction forces act on two different objects, which is why they do not cancel each other out!

Why does a fisherman lean back when pulling a net?

When a fisherman pulls the net, they pull on each other! He must lean back so the net doesn't drag him forward.
When a boatman pushes water backward with a paddle, the water pushes the boat forward—making it move!
When a paddle pushes water backward, it drives the boat forward! Pushing the water makes the water push the boat forward in return.

Draw a book and table separately. Label the upward force of table on book and the equal downward force of book on table: an action–reaction pair on different objects. The book’s weight is Earth pulling the book; its partner is the book pulling Earth, not the table’s upward force.
A force diagram can represent action-reaction pairs by drawing arrows that show the direction and strength of each force on the two interacting objects.
An electric current flowing in a metal wire is really just electrons moving along together!
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, letting electrons flow through and light up a bulb!
Never touch an exposed wire with wet hands! Water lowers your skin's electrical resistance, which increases your shock risk.

Why doesn't an insulator conduct electricity?

An insulator's electrons are tightly held in place, so they cannot move freely to carry electricity!
Ohm's law says current in a circuit equals voltage divided by resistance! It's a simple math rule: I = V/R.

What is the formula for Ohm's law?

It is V = IR! This means voltage (V) equals current (I) times resistance (R).
Ohm's law says current in a circuit equals voltage divided by resistance! It's a simple math rule: I = V/R.

What is the formula for Ohm's law?

It is V = IR! This means voltage (V) equals current (I) times resistance (R).
When you connect batteries end-to-end in series, their voltages add up to give a much stronger push!
In a series circuit, the bulbs or resistors share the battery's voltage. Adding more of them makes each light dimmer!
In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full battery voltage! The bulbs stay bright even when more of them are added.
Adding more branches to a parallel circuit gives the current more paths to flow! Because of this, the total resistance goes down.
In a series circuit, the bulbs or resistors share the battery's voltage. Adding more of them makes each light dimmer!
In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full battery voltage! The bulbs stay bright even when more of them are added.

How do we draw a battery in a circuit diagram?

A cell is drawn as a long line (positive!) and a short line (negative!). Several cells in series? That's alternating long-short-long-short lines!

With a teacher, draw and assemble a low-voltage battery, switch and lamp circuit. Keep the switch open while connecting. Put an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across a lamp. Compare series and parallel loads, recording current and voltage as resistance changes. Never connect this experiment to a wall outlet.
A voltmeter connects in parallel to measure voltage, while an ammeter connects in series! Their connection methods are completely opposite.
We measure current using an ammeter! It connects right into the loop's path so current passes through it, showing in amperes how much electricity is flowing.

A series circuit has only one path for current! If just one part breaks, all the lights go out together.

Why do two bulbs glow dimly when placed in series with one battery?

Both glow dimly because the added resistance reduces the current flowing through each bulb!
In a parallel circuit, each branch works independently! If one bulb or appliance fails, the rest keep working normally.
In a parallel circuit, each branch receives the full battery voltage! The bulbs stay bright even when more of them are added.

Electromagnetic waves are produced when an electric charge changes its motion or speeds up! This happens when electrons vibrate back and forth inside an antenna.
To make a radio wave, a transmitter pushes electrons back and forth in a metal antenna. This wiggling sends out the wave! At the other end, the wave wiggles electrons in the receiver's antenna.

Vibrating electric charges can emit electromagnetic waves. In a wave traveling through empty space, the electric and magnetic fields oscillate perpendicular to its travel direction and to each other: a transverse wave. Unlike sound, it does not need matter to carry it.
Did you know? Light waves can travel through the empty vacuum of outer space without needing any physical medium!
Sunlight travels through the empty vacuum of outer space to reach Earth! Light doesn't need a physical medium to travel.
Radio waves have the lowest frequency in the entire electromagnetic spectrum!
In the spectrum order, microwaves sit right between radio waves and infrared!
In the spectrum order, microwaves sit right between radio waves and infrared!
In the electromagnetic spectrum, microwaves sit right between radio waves and infrared!
In the spectrum order, microwaves sit right between radio waves and infrared!
In the electromagnetic spectrum, microwaves sit right between radio waves and infrared!
Out of all the visible colors, red light has the longest wavelength!
On the flip side, violet has the shortest wavelength among all our visible colors!

Where do X-rays sit in the spectrum order?

They sit right between ultraviolet and gamma rays!

What is the band just beyond violet light?

It's ultraviolet! It has a shorter wavelength than visible light.

Where do X-rays sit in the spectrum order?

They sit right between ultraviolet and gamma rays!
From longest to shortest wavelength, the electromagnetic spectrum order is: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, and gamma!
Gamma rays have the highest frequency in the entire electromagnetic spectrum!
Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength in the entire electromagnetic spectrum!

What happens to the wavelength when frequency goes up?

As frequency increases from radio to gamma rays, the wavelength gets shorter and shorter!
A microwave is the radio wave's younger sibling! Both are electromagnetic, but microwaves have shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies, powering GPS, satellites, and ovens!
The radio uses radio waves! These invisible waves travel through the air to send sound and messages without wires.
Radio waves are invisible helpers! They are a special part of the spectrum that carry signals for our radio, TV, and cellphones.

What did the first famous X-ray photo show?

The bones of Roentgen's wife's hand!
Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895! We use them today to take pictures of bones inside the body.
Gamma rays pack the shortest wavelength and highest energy in the spectrum! They come from nuclear changes and help doctors treat cancer and sterilize hospital tools.
Gamma rays are the highest-energy electromagnetic radiation! They come from radioactive nuclei and are used in cancer treatment (radiation therapy), but large doses are dangerous.
Ultraviolet light from the sun causes sunburn, which makes our skin turn red and get damaged!
Sunscreen protects your skin by absorbing or reflecting harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun before it damages cells!

Read a CDC radiation-health reference and record its date. X-rays and gamma rays are ionizing radiation and can damage cells. Radio waves are non-ionizing; their hazards differ. Ultraviolet exposure can damage skin and eyes. Harm depends on radiation type, intensity and exposure, so do not label every electromagnetic wave equally dangerous.
Matching fossils of animals and plants are found on separate continents, proving they were once connected!

Why do we find the same ancient fossils on continents far apart?

Identical fossils of the same ancient plants and animals are found on far-apart continents, showing that these lands were once joined together!
The coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces — a clue they were once joined!
The Appalachian Mountains in North America line up perfectly with the Caledonian Mountains in Scotland when the continents are rejoined!
Matching fossils of animals and plants are found on separate continents, proving they were once connected!

Why do we find the same ancient fossils on continents far apart?

Identical fossils of the same ancient plants and animals are found on far-apart continents, showing that these lands were once joined together!

Which two large plates squeeze the Philippines?

The Philippines is squeezed right between two large plates: the Philippine Sea Plate and the Eurasian Plate!
Scientists use GPS instruments to measure how the Philippine plates move a few centimeters each year!
Deep ocean trenches are topographical evidence of plate boundaries because they form where one plate slides beneath another!
Scientists map plate boundaries by plotting where volcanoes and earthquakes cluster. The Philippines shows a very clear pattern!
Deep ocean trenches are topographical evidence of plate boundaries because they form where one plate slides beneath another!
The Philippine Trench lies along the eastern side of the Philippines, hidden beneath the Pacific Ocean!

There are three plate boundaries: convergent — plates collide and one subducts or land crunches up; divergent — plates move apart and new crust forms; transform — plates slide horizontally past each other with no crust created or destroyed.
At a divergent boundary, two plates pull apart! Magma rises from below, cools down, and forms brand new crust.

What happens when plates crash into each other?

At a convergent boundary, plates push and collide! This creates tall mountains, deep trenches, and lots of earthquakes and volcanoes.

There are three plate boundaries: convergent — plates collide and one subducts or land crunches up; divergent — plates move apart and new crust forms; transform — plates slide horizontally past each other with no crust created or destroyed.

There are three plate boundaries: convergent — plates collide and one subducts or land crunches up; divergent — plates move apart and new crust forms; transform — plates slide horizontally past each other with no crust created or destroyed.
At a transform boundary, plates slide and grind past each other sideways! This rough rubbing often causes strong earthquakes.
Scientists know what lived in each era by studying fossils! These are found in different layers of rock.
Thousands of layers of sedimentary rock full of fossils give us evidence of the very long history of changing life on Earth.

How do index fossils help scientists?

An index fossil comes from a widespread organism that lived for a short time. It acts as a guide to determine the age of its rock layer!

How do some fossils help tell the age of rocks?

Fossils that were widespread but lived only for a short time are used as markers to tell the age of the rock they are found in!
In an undisturbed stack of rock layers, the oldest layer sits at the bottom and the youngest is on top — that's the law of superposition!
Absolute dating adds real numbers to the relative order of rock layers, turning a simple sequence into a time scale of millions of years!
Scientists estimate Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, based on radiometric dating of the oldest known meteorites and moon rocks!
Absolute dating adds real numbers to the relative order of rock layers, turning a simple sequence into a time scale of millions of years!
Scientists discover a rock's age using radioactive dating, which measures the decay of radioactive elements inside the rock!

How do rocks tell time?

A half-life is the time for half a radioactive isotope to decay. Since this rate is constant, it acts as a natural clock to measure rock age!
The geologic time scale organizes Earth's history into chunks: eons, eras, periods, and epochs — from the longest stretches down to the shortest!

How is Earth's long history divided?

In the geologic time scale, it is divided into eons, eras, periods, and epochs!
The geologic time scale organizes Earth's history into chunks: eons, eras, periods, and epochs — from the longest stretches down to the shortest!
The time scale shows the Moon formed very early, about 4.5 billion years ago, right after Earth itself took shape!
The Lehmann discontinuity is the boundary between the liquid outer core and solid inner core, found by studying P-wave behavior!
The inner core was discovered when a faint P-wave appeared in the shadow zone, showing that the solid inner core reflects waves!

How do scientists know the outer core is liquid?

S-waves cannot pass through liquid! Since they stop at the outer core, it proves the outer core is liquid.

How do scientists know Earth has a liquid outer core?

S waves (transverse seismic waves) cannot pass through liquid! After earthquakes, the absence of S waves in certain zones proved that Earth has a liquid outer core.
We can't drill deep into the Earth, so scientists use earthquake seismic waves like an x-ray to see the layers inside!
The Lehmann discontinuity is the boundary between the liquid outer core and solid inner core, found by studying P-wave behavior!
Planet Earth is made of 4 main layers: the crust, the mantle, the outer core, and the inner core!

Use a USGS reference and scale 1 cm = 1,000 km: Earth’s radius is about 6.37 cm on paper. Mark the core boundary at about 2.9 cm depth and the inner core at about 5.15 cm depth; the outer core lies between. Add the thin crust above the mantle. In a separate mechanical overlay, label lithosphere as crust plus rigid uppermost mantle, and asthenosphere beneath it. These overlap the composition layers; do not add them as extra thicknesses.

An asteroid is made of rock and metal, while a comet is made of ice, dust, and rock!
Comets are made of ice and dust—they grow a tail near the Sun! Asteroids are rockier and metallic, with no tail at all.
A meteoroid is a cool rock floating in space that has not yet entered Earth's atmosphere!

Where do asteroids and meteoroids come from?

Many are leftover pieces from when the Solar System formed billions of years ago!
An asteroid is made of rock and metal, while a comet is made of ice, dust, and rock!
Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and is also considered a dwarf planet!
Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and is also considered a dwarf planet!
A dwarf planet orbits the Sun and is round from its own gravity. But it hasn't cleared its orbit of other objects, so it's not a full planet!

Where do asteroids and meteoroids come from?

Many are leftover pieces from when the Solar System formed billions of years ago!
Scientists study asteroids and comets because they barely changed in billions of years, acting like "fossils" that preserve our solar system's formation history!

Why do some meteor showers happen at the exact same time every year?

It's because Earth passes through the same comet-debris path during each orbit!

Where do meteor showers like the Perseids and Leonids come from?

Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through a comet's debris trail! The Perseids in August come from Comet Swift-Tuttle, and the Leonids in November come from Comet Tempel-Tuttle.

NASA’s meteor reference explains recurring showers as Earth crossing streams of debris left along orbits, often by comets. Use the source to connect the yearly return to Earth’s orbit, not a star falling toward us. Visibility and strength vary with the debris, weather and sky conditions; a calendar date is not a guarantee of a bright display.
Many annual showers are visible from the Philippines! Some northern radiants sit lower, but a local astronomy club table is a super useful source.
The Hubble Space Telescope orbits above Earth's atmosphere, so it can see space super clearly!
Scientists use powerful telescopes like James Webb to spot very distant galaxies and study the young universe!
A space probe is a robotic spacecraft with no people on board, sent to explore faraway planets too dangerous or distant for humans!

How do scientists study the Sun's super-hot corona?

NASA's Parker Solar Probe flies closer to the Sun than any spacecraft in history! It entered the corona to help scientists understand why it's hotter than the surface.

What shape is DNA?

DNA is shaped like a twisted ladder — scientists call it a 'double helix'!

What shape is DNA?

DNA is shaped like a double helix — imagine a ladder that's been twisted round and round!

Build a paper model of the DNA double helix: two sugar–phosphate backbones form the sides. Label the base-pair rungs A–T and C–G, then twist the ladder gently. The order of bases stores information; the model shows structure, not DNA’s actual size or all its chemical detail.
The two DNA strands are held by weak hydrogen bonds between paired bases, so the ladder can unzip when the cell copies it!

What exactly is a gene?

A gene is a segment of DNA that gives instructions for a trait, like the color of your eyes.
Your DNA is neatly packed into structures called chromosomes, found inside a cell's nucleus. Each chromosome carries many genes.

What exactly is a gene?

A gene is a segment of DNA that gives instructions for a trait, like the color of your eyes.
Blood type — A, B, AB, or O — is determined by genes from your parents. It's an inherited trait that can't be changed.
Half of your chromosomes come from your mother, and the other half come from your father.

What is a mutation?

A mutation is a change in DNA — it might do nothing, help, or hurt the living thing that has it!

What causes mutations in DNA?

Mutations can be caused by things like radiation and certain chemicals that damage DNA.

What causes mutations in DNA?

Mutations can be caused by things like radiation and certain chemicals that damage DNA.

What causes DNA mutations?

UV light, radiation, certain chemicals, or even random copying errors when DNA duplicates itself can all cause mutations.

What causes mutations in DNA?

Mutations can be caused by things like radiation and certain chemicals that damage DNA.

What causes DNA mutations?

UV light, radiation, certain chemicals, or even random copying errors when DNA duplicates itself can all cause mutations.

A mutation changes DNA sequence; chromosome changes can affect larger pieces. The NHGRI mutation reference lists copying errors, mutagens and viral infection among possible causes. Some infectious agents can alter host DNA; this does not mean every infection causes an inherited mutation. Radiation and certain chemicals can also damage DNA.
Not all mutations are harmful — some are neutral with no effect, some are harmful like those causing cancer, and some are beneficial and help organisms survive.

Use a reliable genetics textbook to compare beneficial, harmful and neutral mutation effects. A DNA change that does not alter a protein’s function may be neutral. Another can disrupt a needed function; another may improve survival in a particular environment. Classify effects using evidence about the organism and conditions, not the word mutation alone.

Is a mutation always bad?

No! A mutation is a change in an organism's DNA, and it can be harmless, harmful, or even helpful for survival.
Not all mutations are harmful — some are neutral with no effect, some are harmful like those causing cancer, and some are beneficial and help organisms survive.

High biodiversity can improve ecosystem resilience: several species performing related roles may respond differently to drought, disease or food shortages. If one declines, another may maintain part of that function. This is a buffer, not a guarantee; severe stress can still damage a diverse ecosystem.
In a diverse grassland, different grasses grow in different seasons! The soil stays covered all year, preventing erosion.

Why is an ecosystem with many species tougher?

When many different species do the same job — like many kinds of insects that pollinate flowers — there's a backup if one disappears. That's why ecosystems with many species are more stable than ones with only a few!

The tamaraw is a small kind of buffalo found only on the island of Mindoro — and it is critically endangered.
The Palawan pangolin is critically endangered because of heavy poaching for its scales and meat, illegally traded across Asia.

The Philippine eagle is critically endangered from forest loss and hunting — that's why the law forbids anyone from shooting it.
When a species goes extinct, its ecosystem services like pollination or pest control are lost, and people lose food and medicine sources!
Crocodiles in the Philippines are protected by law because they're at risk of disappearing forever.
The narra is protected by law and can't be freely cut down because it's becoming rare in our forests.

Compare reliable local environmental reports about deforestation, pollution and invasive species. Record the source, place, date, affected organisms and evidence for each claim. For conservation, match the action to the threat: protect habitat from clearing, reduce pollutant inputs, or ask trained authorities to manage an invasive species. Do not release or collect wildlife for this task.

Why is the forest floor so dark?

In a tropical rainforest, the thick canopy of leaves at the top blocks almost all sunlight, making the ground dark!

Label biotic organisms and abiotic conditions: tropical rainforest—trees and rainfall; swamp—trees and flooded soil; estuary—fish and changing salinity; mangrove forest—mangrove roots and tidal water; coral reef—coral animals and sunlight. Arrows can show dependence, such as plants using light. A coral is an animal, not an abiotic rock.

Yes! It is a chemical change because the atoms are rearranged into a brand new substance with new properties.
When new bonds form, no atoms are lost or created! They just rearrange, keeping the same elements before and after.

What happens when an atom loses or gains an electron?

It becomes charged and is called an ion!
When an atom loses electrons, it becomes a positively charged ion called a cation! A great example is the sodium ion, Na⁺.

How does an ionic bond form?

When a metal atom GIVES its electron to a nonmetal atom! After this, both become charged and attract each other.

How do atoms stick together in table salt?

In an ionic bond, one atom gives electrons to another, giving them opposite charges that attract—like sodium and chlorine in sodium chloride!

What is the chemical formula of table salt?

The chemical formula of table salt is NaCl!
The chemical formula for the table salt you use is NaCl, which stands for sodium and chlorine!

Where does the name magnesium oxide come from?

It gets its name from its ions: magnesium (Mg2+) and oxide (O2-), with the metal name first!

They are hard solids with very high melting points because the pull between their opposite ions is super strong!
